messages:
sami: Quick heads-up, saw an OOM-ish incident on the canary pods during the continuous-batcher rollout. Trace looks KV-heavy rather than pure token volume.

eva: ugh, timeline? was that after the kernel-selector change? :thinking:

sami: yes — happened ~11:43 UTC right after we flipped the kernel-route heuristic that biases fp16 kernels for long sequences. stack shows slow eviction + a big KV cache spike.

liam: can you paste the short profile? rough numbers are fine.

sami: perf snapshot:
```
2026-03-15T11:43:21Z canary-3  GPU mem used 17192MB -> spikes to 24560MB
kv-cache footprint estimate: +7.2MB per request avg (heavy tail)
batch token budget: 1536 -> batch built with 18 requests, avg seq 512
kernel handoff time: +12ms on route change
eviction/wait stalls: 80ms per batch
```

tilly: that avg +7.2MB/request KV is wild — is that from many prefix prompts with long histories?

sami: yep many chat continuations with long KV contexts and a few embeddings-based reranks in the mix. The batching admittance had no KV footprint estimate so it allowed too many KV-heavy items into the batch.

eva: sounds like we need an admission prioritizer that accounts for estimated KV size in the token budget. i mocked a tiny config for prioritizer scoring: 
```
admission_policy: prioritized
score = w_tokens*norm_tokens + w_kv*norm_kv_est + w_latency*pred_latency
kv_est = prompt_tokens * kv_per_token_coeff + static_prefix_kv
```

liam: agree. we should keep admission budget in two dims: "compute token budget" and "kv-resident-bytes budget". admission only succeeds if both budgets hold.

perf-bot: Canary metric alert: canary-3 evictions/sec spike >3x for 120s at 2026-03-15T11:43:30Z

tilly: conservative immediate fix: clamp max-batch-count when avg_kv_est > threshold and prefer short-seq requests (demote long + kv-heavy). This buys time while we iterate on estimator.

sami: implemented quick clamp (rollout to canary). config snippet used: 
```
batch_max_count: 12
kv_est_threshold_mb: 4.0
priority_demote: {kv_heavy: 0.6, long_seq: 0.7}
```

eva: nice. do we have a cheap estimator for kv_per_token_coeff? maybe historical average per model + small multiplier.

sami: i used moving 99th pct of recent requests per model; cheap and conservative. reduced canary OOMs immediately.

liam: longer term: we should export KV footprint signals from the router into the profiler and make kernel selection aware of KV pressure. kernel selection currently only looks at seq len and model family -> we saw handoff latency increase because chosen kernel had larger scratch+KV interaction.

tilly: also consider admission aging: if a request sits in queue longer, its estimated KV may be stale (prefixes could have been evicted), so re-evaluate before admit.

sami: good point. I saw few requests that waited 120ms and then evicted pieces and changed footprint. recheck reduces over-conservative demotions.

eva: action items: 1) stabilize estimator (sami) 2) dual-budget admission (liam) 3) kernel-selector KV-awareness POC (tilly) 4) add perf-bot alert for kv-eviction-rate (perf)

liam: i'll start a tiny PR for dual-budget admission. will add unit tests for corner cases (race between eviction and admit).

sami: will push estimator curve and canary metrics. will also pin canary kernel-route to old behavior until kernel-handshakes are KV-safe.

perf-bot: Deployment note: canary clamp config rolled out at 2026-03-15T11:59:02Z to canary-3

tilly: thanks all. nice fast triage. we'll reconvene after liam/sami PRs land. :thumbsup:
